title: fix(formula)!: the formula gate refuses bare date subtraction, which reads null or {} at runtime
body:
domain:server#2 · os-project-manager · session_0186vfjHHMsRXC9EUT9hTFMo

<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-project-manager"} -->
_Requested by **Leehom** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1X?thread=cmsg_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1X4sWB7ZcgNfe6fa1hN24t8N)_

Fixes #28944

Clause-②: yes (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: narrowed
Skills-docs: follow-up #29061 — `skills/objectstack-formula/SKILL.md` (the "No date arithmetic" callout says `end - start` "does not fault — it yields a `duration` stored as `{}`"; after this change it is refused at build, and it read null at runtime), `skills/objectstack-ui/evals/analytics-inline-vs-dataset.json` id 6 (its prompt describes a stored `end_date - start_date` formula). `skills/**` is a Tier H surface outside this claim's file surface, so it is not edited here. `content/docs/data-modeling/formulas.mdx` is updated here.

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么**：公式里直接相减两个日期字段（`record.end_date - record.start_date`），或用当前时间减日期字段（`today() - record.start_date`），现在在 `os validate` / `os build` / `os lint` 和保存对象时都会报错（保存为 422 `expression-invalid`），错误信息说明运行时会读成 null 或 `{}`，并给出 `daysBetween(a, b)` 的改法。datetime 字段同样处理。
- **为什么改**：运行时日期字段是文本（`YYYY-MM-DD` 或 ISO 时间），不是时间戳；两个文本相减会报错，字段每条记录都读成 null；时间戳减日期得到一个时长，字段读成 `{}`。以前的检查把日期字段当时间戳，所以放行了这两种写法，构建全绿、线上空值。
- **风险与回滚**：这是一次收窄（`Metadata-protocol: narrowed`），formula 与 spec 升 minor。被拒的公式本来每条记录都是 null 或 `{}`，没有能用的写法会被拒；本仓库 packages、examples 和 hotcrm 里没有这种公式。`(end - start) + 1` 原有的报错一字不变。回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- **先看**：`packages/formula/src/cel-engine.ts`（`firstDateTextVerdict` 与 `registerDateTextOverloads`：日期字段按运行时文本声明的类型和它被允许的运算）、`packages/formula/src/validate.ts`（`dateTextIssue`：两种拒绝及其文案）、`packages/formula/src/validate-date-text-arithmetic.test.ts`（每一行同时问检查和运行时）。
- **两分钟验证**：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/formula exec vitest run src/validate-date-text-arithmetic.test.ts`，预期 27 个用例全绿。
- **需要你做的**：无，席位落地。

## What changes

- **`@objectstack/formula`**
  - New `firstDateTextVerdict(source, fieldCelTypes, scope)` in `cel-engine.ts` (package-internal, not on the entry). It type-checks the expression with every `date` / `datetime` field declared as `DateText`, the text the runtime actually holds, instead of the Timestamp `firstTypeMismatch` declares. `registerDateTextOverloads` declares, for that check-only env, exactly the overloads the evaluator answers on that text, each measured through `celEngine.evaluate`: ordering and equality against another date field, a text literal or a Timestamp (`bool`), `Timestamp - DateText` and `DateText - Timestamp` (`Duration`, since the evaluator coerces the text against a Timestamp), and `+` with text (concatenation). Everything else on the text faults the check exactly where it faults the evaluator: `DateText - DateText`, `DateText + int`, `DateText - Duration`, `Timestamp + DateText`. Nothing is matched in the source text. The verdict falls out of the typing.
  - `validateExpression` asks `firstTypeMismatch` first, unchanged. Only when that passes does `dateTextIssue` ask `firstDateTextVerdict`. So every shape the gate already refused keeps its code, params and words. That includes the `+ 1` shape (`date-arithmetic`, `google.protobuf.Duration + int`).
  - Two new codes in the closed refusal set, both errors:
    - `date-text-arithmetic` (`params: { operands, reference? }`): arithmetic on a date field's text that the evaluator faults on, in any role. `record.end_date - record.start_date` reads null, and so does a predicate `record.end_date - record.start_date > duration("72h")`.
    - `date-duration-value` (`params: { reference? }`): a formula (`value` role) whose computed type is `google.protobuf.Duration`, which a field reads as `{}`. `today() - record.start_date`, `now() - record.start_at`, and also `today() - daysAgo(3)`: the verdict reads the computed type, not whether a date field is named. A predicate that compares a duration (`today() - record.start_date > duration("72h")`) evaluates and is untouched.
  - The pass runs when the hint carries `fieldTypes` (as before) and there is something to find: a date field to retype, or a `value` whose type is the question.
- **`@objectstack/spec`**: ADR-0087 D3 entry `formula-date-subtraction-refused` (`migrations/entries/semantic/18.formula-date-subtraction-refused.ts`), with the FROM → TO and why there is no mechanical rewrite.
- `content/docs/data-modeling/formulas.mdx`: a "Date subtraction" row in the type-soundness table.
- No change in `@objectstack/lint` source. Its formula pass (`validateExpression('value', …, { fieldTypes, scope: 'record' })`) and every object-bound predicate site already hand the validator the field types. So `os validate`, `os build`, `os lint` and the runtime authoring gate behind the object save door (`runRuntimeAuthoringRules`) all answer from the one judge. A lint test pins the stack face.

### Measured before building

- **Shipped formulas** (`packages/**`, `examples/**`, `skills/**`, `content/**` at `135054eb`; hotcrm `origin/main` at `d4ffe99`): a grep for a date field, `today()` or `now()` on either side of a minus finds no formula that subtracts dates. The only hits are number subtraction (`record.budget - …`, `record.fee - record.tax`) and doc prose. hotcrm's 15 formula fields subtract no date (one uses `daysBetween(record.stage_entry_date, today())`), and its seeds' `now() - duration('Nh')` are seed values, not gate input. No shipped formula is refused.
- **Datetime** (live, `os dev --fresh` on `examples/app-todo` with a probe object, main `135054eb`, sqlite-wasm): `record.end_at - record.start_at` reads `null` with the same WARN, `no such overload: dyn‹string› - dyn‹string›` (the SQL driver serves a datetime as ISO text on every dialect). `now() - record.start_at` reads `{}`. So datetime is included, per the ruling.

## Tests

- `packages/formula/src/validate-date-text-arithmetic.test.ts` (new, 27). A table where each row is judged twice: by `celEngine.evaluate` over the row a read door serves (dates as text), and by `validateExpression`. It pins that the gate refuses exactly what reads `null` or `{}` and nothing the evaluator answers. Refused rows: the card's two shapes, both datetime shapes, `record.start_date - today()`, the subtraction inside a comparison, and `record.start_date - duration("24h")`. Controls: `daysBetween` (both forms), comparing a duration, `(today() - record.start_date).getHours()`, date ordering against a date, `today()`, `now()` and a literal, equality, the null guard, concatenation, `addDays`, and number subtraction. Further tests: the `+ 1` shape keeps `date-arithmetic` with `google.protobuf.Duration + int`; the flattened (flow) scope; `date-duration-value` is `value`-role only; no `fieldTypes` means no check.
- `packages/formula/src/expression-refusal-codes.test.ts`: pins for both codes (code, params, full message), and two sweep sources, so both arms are provoked and their params are checked against the message. The existing `date-arithmetic` pins pass unchanged.
- `packages/formula/src/validate.test.ts`: `record.end_date - record.start_date` leaves the "runtime-tolerated" list, where it was pinned as clean ("→ Duration, no further arith"). That pin is the behaviour this PR reverses.
- `packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.test.ts`: `validateStackExpressions` refuses `qa_span_bare` and `qa_since_today` at their `expression`, as errors, and leaves `qa_span_daysbetween` clean.

- `validate-date-text-arithmetic.test.ts`: **10 failed, 17 passed**. The failures are the seven refused rows, the naming test, the flattened test and the role test. Every control row and the `+ 1` test pass on base.

Live red, same base, CLI face: `os validate`, `os lint` and `os build` all exit 0 on the probe object, and REST answers `qa_span_bare: null`, `qa_span_daysbetween: 4`, `qa_since_today: {}`, `qa_dt_span: null`, `qa_dt_since_now: {}`.

<details><summary>Ablation: each half reds only its own cases</summary>

Both through `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor hit 1 → 0, blob restored == HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty), formula read from `src/`, three suites (`validate-date-text-arithmetic`, `expression-refusal-codes`, `validate`).

1. Drop the text typing (`cel-engine.ts`, `temporalAsText && t === 'timestamp' ? DATE_TEXT_CEL_TYPE` → `String(temporalAsText) === 'ablated' ? DATE_TEXT_CEL_TYPE`, blob `d48b48384db5` → `0157c4c635ea`): **8 failed, 180 passed**. These are the four `date-text-arithmetic` rows, the naming and flattened tests, the `date-text-arithmetic` pin and the sweep. Every `date-duration-value` row stays green, because the Timestamp typing also computes `Duration` for those, and the controls and `+ 1` stay green.
2. Drop the duration-value arm (`validate.ts`, `if (role !== 'value' || verdict.type !== 'google.protobuf.Duration') return null;` → `if (String(role) !== 'ablated') return null;`, blob `787a1532d20b` → `b6de2a9964e0`): **7 failed, 181 passed**. These are the three `date-duration-value` rows, the naming and role tests, the `date-duration-value` pin and the sweep. The controls stay green.

</details>

## Acceptance notes

- **The `+ 1` case keeps its words** by ordering, not by special-casing. The Timestamp typing answers first and is unchanged. Under the text typing alone, `(end - start) + 1` would fault first at the inner subtraction.
- **`date-duration-value` is wider than the two named shapes.** Any formula whose computed type is a Duration is refused, `today() - daysAgo(3)` included, because that is what the typing answers and every such value reads `{}`. No shipped formula has that shape either.
- **Masking stays conservative.** The text-typed check reports only an arithmetic fault with `DateText` on a side. Any other first fault, such as `isoDate(record.d)` (which the evaluator refuses on text too), returns no verdict, so it can only miss a later fault in the same expression. It never invents one.
- **Message subject**: when two date fields are named, `reference` is the first one the object declares that appears in the source, the same best-effort attribution `firstTypeMismatch` uses.
- **`@objectstack/rest` bundles a copy of `@objectstack/formula`** into its `dist` (found while rebuilding for the live probe). The copy follows on its next build. This was noted, not changed, and is not filed.
- Not merged with `origin/main` before opening: the 16 commits since `135054eb` touch no file under `packages/formula`, `packages/lint` or `packages/spec/src/migrations`, and GitHub reports the merge. The merge queue tests the merged tree.
